title: NEWTRAL Ergonomic Chairs Compared: Which One Fits Your Setup?
metaDescription: Comparing four NEWTRAL ergonomic chairs — MAGICH003, MagicH-BPro, Freedom-X criss-cross, and NT002 — plus where the flagship MagicH-GPRO fits in the lineup.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: NEWTRAL's whole catalog revolves around one patented idea — a backrest and lumbar system that auto-follows your posture instead of locking into a fixed recline. Once you get past that shared core, the lineup splits into genuinely different chairs: a budget auto-following model, a footrest-equipped mid-tier, an unconventional criss-cross floor-style seat, and a premium all-adjustable flagship. We already covered the top-of-line [MagicH-GPRO in a dedicated review](/blog/newtral-magich-gpro-ergonomic-chair-review-2026/) — this guide is about everything else in the range and which one actually fits your setup.

items.label: MAGICH003 — Core Feature
items.value: Auto-following backrest, adjustable headrest & seat depth, 3D armrest — no footrest

items.label: MagicH-BPro — Core Feature
items.value: Same auto-following system as MAGICH003, adds a foldable footrest, 4 lockable recline positions

items.label: Freedom-X-FB — Core Feature
items.value: Criss-cross "pretzel" seated posture, built-in laptop tray, multi-posture recliner — not a traditional chair shape at all

items.label: NT002 — Core Feature
items.value: Adjustable armrest, headrest, and footrest together — the most fully-adjustable model outside the GPRO

pros: Every model shares the same core auto-following lumbar mechanism — you're not getting a worse back-support system by buying the cheaper MAGICH003
The MagicH-BPro's foldable footrest adds genuine recline-and-relax usability without the GPRO's full price tag
The Freedom-X-FB's criss-cross seated posture is a legitimately different option for people who find traditional chair postures uncomfortable over long sessions, not just a novelty shape
The NT002's fully adjustable armrest, headrest, and footrest together makes it the most tunable chair in the range short of the GPRO itself
Detachable workstation desktop attachments are available for several models, useful for a laptop-and-coffee setup without a separate desk
cons: The MAGICH003 has no footrest — if recline-and-relax matters to you, step up to the BPro or NT002
The Freedom-X-FB's floor-style criss-cross posture is a genuinely different way of sitting — don't buy it expecting a standard office chair feel, try to understand the posture style first
None of these four quite match the GPRO's 5D headrest and 4D armrest adjustability — that extra range is specifically what the flagship price pays for
Heavier units (BPro, NT002) take real assembly effort and floor space, same trade-off as the GPRO

items.question: Which NEWTRAL chair should I buy?
items.answer: Budget and core back support only: MAGICH003. Want a footrest for breaks without paying flagship price: MagicH-BPro. Prefer a cross-legged, relaxed seated posture over a traditional chair shape: Freedom-X-FB. Want near-flagship adjustability without the GPRO's full cost: NT002. If budget isn't the constraint and you want the most adjustable option NEWTRAL makes, the MagicH-GPRO is still the one to get — see our full review for that model specifically.

items.question: Do the cheaper NEWTRAL chairs have the same lumbar support as the GPRO?
items.answer: The core auto-following mechanism is shared across the MAGICH003, BPro, and GPRO — the lumbar tracking technology itself isn't downgraded on the cheaper models. What changes between tiers is adjustability range (headrest, armrest, recline positions) and extras like the footrest, not the fundamental back-support mechanism.

items.question: Is the criss-cross Freedom-X chair actually comfortable for work?
items.answer: It depends entirely on whether you're comfortable sitting cross-legged for extended periods — it's genuinely a different posture, not a gimmick shape. People who already prefer sitting cross-legged on a couch or floor tend to find it a natural, relaxed alternative to a traditional chair. People who've never sat that way for long stretches should expect an adjustment period, or may simply prefer a conventional chair shape instead.

items.question: What's the difference between the NT002 and the MagicH-GPRO?
items.answer: Both offer adjustable armrests, headrest, and a footrest, putting the NT002 close to the GPRO on paper. The GPRO's 5D auto-following headrest and 4D armrests (height, depth, width, and 20° rotation) give it a wider adjustment range than the NT002's simpler adjustable set, which is reflected in the price gap between them.

sections.content: The auto-following lumbar system is the constant across NEWTRAL's whole range — what you're actually choosing between is footrest, adjustability range, and in the Freedom-X-FB's case, an entirely different seated posture. Start with the MAGICH003 if budget leads, move to the BPro or NT002 for more adjustability, and only go to the GPRO if you want the widest range NEWTRAL offers and the price fits.
